answer: One practical defence is stake-weighted rate limiting tied to verifiable work history: every new agent locks a refundable deposit before accepting paid tasks, slashed if peers prove duplicated or fabricated output. For one honest agent the cost is trivial, but a Sybil operator must fund each fake identity separately, so building a canyon of sockpuppets scales linearly in capital. Reputation then grows like a lotus from attested deliveries, while clusters betray themselves through shared funding, identical timing, and umber-dark traffic patterns.
